CITY COUNCIL MEETING FOR OCT
http://www.adobe.com/products/acrobat/readstep2.html
THE CITY COUNCIL MEETING FOR OCTOBER 18, 2021 AT 4:30 P.M. WILL TAKE PLACE
SOLELY BY VIDEOCONFERENCE/TELECONFERENCE.
City Council Meeting Policy:
www.cityofpasadena.net/city-clerk/wp-content/uploads/sites/21/City-Council-Meeting-Policy.pdf
In order to facilitate public participation at meetings held solely by
electronic means, the City will accept public comment in the following manner:
1. During the meeting, members of
the public may provide live public comment by submitting a speaker card prior to
the start of public comment on that item, at the following webpage:
www.cityofpasadena.net/city-clerk/public-comment
If a public comment speaker wishes to speak on more than one agenda item, please
indicate so on the online form (multiple item speakers will be handled according
to the process posted on the agenda and as specified in the City Council meeting
policy). Public comments are limited to 3 minutes each, and the Mayor and City
Council may limit this time if reasonable under the circumstances.
2. Speaker Card Help Line :
If a public comment speaker needs assistance in completing a speaker card,
please call the City Clerk’s Office at: (626) 744-4124. Help line will open
30 minutes prior to the
posted start time of the meeting.
After submitting a public speaker card, join the virtual meeting after the
published start time with a computer, other electronic device, or by telephone.
The same name or telephone number on the Speaker Card should be used for the
virtual meeting in order to locate and unmute the speaker.
Your phone call to the City Council
meeting will be recorded as part of the City Council meeting. By
staying on the line and making public comment during the City Council meeting,
you are agreeing to have your phone call recorded.
Computer or electronic devices, join the meeting at:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/161482446
Telephone only dial-in: 1-669-900-6833, Meeting ID: 161 482 446
3. Members of the public may
submit correspondence of any length prior to the start of the meeting, at the
following email address:
correspondence@cityofpasadena.net
Correspondence will be forwarded to the City Council prior to the start of the
meeting, posted online, and made part of the legislative record for the item.

LA REUNIÓN DEL CONSEJO MUNICIPAL DEL 18 DE OCTUBRE DE 2021 A LAS 4:30 P.M.
TENDRÁ LUGAR ÚNICAMENTE POR VIDEOCONFERENCIA/TELECONFERENCIA.
City Council Meeting Policy:
www.cityofpasadena.net/city-clerk/wp-content/uploads/sites/21/City-Council-Meeting-Policy.pdf
Para facilitar la participación del público en reuniones realizadas únicamente
por medios electrónicos, la Ciudad aceptará comentarios del público de la
siguiente manera:
1. Durante la reunión, los miembros del
público pueden hacer comentarios públicos en vivo presentando una tarjeta de
oratoria antes del inicio del comentario sobre el artículo que se está tratando
en el siguiente sitio web:
www.cityofpasadena.net/city-clerk/public-comment
Si un orador de comentario público desea hablar sobre más de un artículo del
orden del día, le solicitamos que lo indique en el formulario en línea (los
oradores sobre artículos múltiples se manejarán según el proceso publicado en la
agenda y lo especificado en la política sobre las reuniones el Consejo
Municipal). Los comentarios públicos se limitan a 3 minutos cada uno y el
Alcalde y el Consejo Municipal pueden limitar este tiempo si lo consideran
razonable para las circunstancias.
2. Línea
de ayuda de la tarjeta de oratoria pública :
Si un orador de comentario público
necesita asistencia para completar su tarjeta, puede llamar
a la Oficina del
Secretario de la Ciudad al
(626) 744-4124. La línea de ayuda abrirá 30
minutos antes
del inicio de la reunión.
Después de presentar una tarjeta de oratoria pública, únase a la reunión virtual
a la
hora de inicio publicada con una computadora, otro dispositivo electrónico o por
teléfono. Debe usar el
mismo nombre o número de teléfono de la tarjeta de oratoria para la reunión
virtual de modo que se pueda ubicar y habilitar el audio para el
orador.
Su llamada telefónica a la reunión del Concejo
Municipal se grabará como parte de la
reunión del Concejo Municipal. Al permanecer en la línea y hacer
comentarios públicos durante la
reunión del Concejo Municipal, está aceptando que se grabe su llamada
telefónica.
Computadoras y dispositivos electrónicos pueden sumarse a la reunión en:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/161482446
Número para ingresar a la reunión por teléfono: 1-669-900-6833, ID de la
reunión: 161 482 446
3. Los miembros del público
pueden enviar correspondencia de cualquier longitud antes del inicio de
la reunión a la siguiente dirección de correo electrónico:
correspondence@cityofpasadena.net
La
correspondencia se enviará al Consejo Municipal antes del inicio de la reunión,
se publicará en línea, y se incorporará al registro legislativo sobre el
artículo.

  The meeting was convened and held virtually by videoconference/teleconference.

OPENING:  Mayor Gordo called the meeting to order at 4:34 p.m. The pledge
  of allegiance was led by Councilmember Masuda.

CEREMONIAL MATTERS  Tim McDonald, Library Deputy Director, provided information on the
  many contributions made to the City's library system by the Friends
  of the Pasadena Public Library organization, and thanked them for
  all their support. Janice Segall, President of the Friends of the
  Pasadena Public Library, thanked the Mayor, City Council, staff and
  volunteers for their time and work in supporting the City's libraries.
  Mayor Gordo announced a proclamation declaring October 17 - 23,
  2021 as "National Friends of Libraries Week," in the City of
  Pasadena.

  Mayor Gordo presented a proclamation to Manuel Carmona,
  Deputy Director of Public Health, declaring October 2021 as
  "National Long-Term Care Residents' Rights Month" in Pasadena.
  Mr. Carmona representing Pasadena Elderly and Dependant Adult
  Liaison (PEDAL) Committee, spoke on the Committee's work and
  thanked the Mayor, City Council and staff for the recognition.

  Councilmember Williams and Mayor Gordo spoke on the passing
  of long-time Pasadena resident, Myriam Cascella, expressed
  condolences to her family and friends, and asked that the City
  Council meeting be adjourned in her memory.

  Councilmember Kennedy spoke on the life and the passing of
  former United States Secretary of State, Colin Powell, and
  expressed sympathy on his passing.

  Mayor Gordo reported that pursuant to an order by President Biden,
  all government offices in Pasadena will lower the U.S. flags to be
  flown at half-staff in honor of former Secretary of State Powell until
  Friday, October 22, 2021 .

OLD BUSINESS  CONSIDERATION OF DIRECTION RELATED TO GAS-
  POWERED LEAF BLOWING MACHINES
  Recommendation: It is recommended, that following a staff
  presentation and City Council discussion, the City Council either:
  (1) Direct the City Attorney to prepare an ordinance to amend Title
  9 (Public Peace, Morals and Welfare) of the Pasadena Municipal
  Code to prohibit the use of gas-powered leaf blowing machines
  within Pasadena;
  (2) Refer the matter to the Public Safety Committee for further
  consideration;
  (3) Provide City staff with direction on the matter; or
  (4) Take no action.

  City Manager Mermell provided a PowerPoint presentation on the
  item and responded to questions.

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that 54 letters/emails (including one
  letter on behalf of eight community organizations) expressing
  concerns, providing suggestions, and/or stating support for an
  ordinance prohibiting the use of gas powered leaf blowing machines
  in Pasadena, and one letter urging the City Council to vote no
  prohibiting the use of gas powered leaf blowing machines, were
  received by the City Clerk's Office, distributed to the City Council,
  posted on-line, and made part of the public record.

  Councilmember Madison advocated for staff to follow Assembly
  Bill-1346 Air Pollution, which will require states to adopt regulations
  related to gas-powered tools by July 1, 2022 and ban sales by 2024;
  phase out two-stroke engines for gas powered leaf blowing
  machines; and conduct an analysis on the difference of the carbon
  footprint from switching from gas to electric operating leaf blowers.

  Vice Mayor Wilson stated that he believes the matter should be
  agendized at a future Public Safety Committee meeting, and is
  supportive of taking a closer look on the matter. He asked staff to
  provide information on the hardship the new legislation will have on
  small lawn business owners and the City's ability to provide grant
  funds or micro loans for such businesses.

Council Minutes  9  10/ 18/2021
   Councilmember Kennedy asked staff to identify alternatives to
  publically funded programs where business owners can turn in gas
  powered leaf blowers for destruction and the City can provide a
  rebate for a portion of costs associated with purchasing leaf blowers
  that emit the least amount of noise and carbon dioxide.

  Mayor Gordo advocated for staff and organizations such as the
  Pasadena Community Foundation to raise funds for grants that
  would support a City replacement program for gas powered leaf
  blowers in Pasadena, and an ordinance banning the use of gas
  powered leaf blowers. He also recommended that the matter be
  agendized at a future Public Safety Committee meeting.

  The following individuals spoke in favor of banning gas powered
  leaf blowers, and provided comments:

  Jill Shook, representing Making Housing and Community
  Happen (MHCH)
  Cheryl Auger, Pasadena resident
  Wes Reutimann, Pasadena resident
  Anthony Manousos, representing MHCH
  Una Lee Jost, Pasadena resident

  Councilmember Williams advocated for staff to return to the City
  Council with an ordinance banning gas powered leaf blowers, and
  recommended that staff look at the South Pasadena ordinance as
  a model. She asked staff to include in the ordinance regulations
  phasing out the use of gas powered leaf blowers by a certain date,
  and provide education seminars and any available rebate
  information to the public. In addition, she advocated to limit the use
  of electric leaf blowers to walkways only to avoid blowing
  contaminants into the environment. Council member Williams stated
  that she believes the City should set an example to the community
  by using electric leaf blowers on City properties.

  Vice Mayor Wilson requested information on the benefits of limiting
  the use of electric leaf blowers and asked staff to look at both the
  gas and electric leaf blowers in a comprehensive review of the City's
  current and proposed ordinances.

  Following discussion, on the order of the Mayor, and consensus of
  the City Council, Mayor Gordo will work with staff to determine
  which Committee of the City Council the matter will be agendized
  for review and additional consideration.

  On order of the Mayor, the meeting recessed at 6:40 p.m. and
  reconvened at 6:43 p.m.

FROM OFFICERS AND  IMPLEMENTATION
DEPARTMENTS  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council receive
  this report on the relationship between State housing legislation and
  the City's ongoing efforts to implement the 2015 General Plan and
  provide further direction to the Planning and Community
  Development Department on carrying out key citywide goals and
  policies.

  City Manager Mermell provided introductory comments, and David
  Reyes, Director of Planning, presented a PowerPoint presentation
  on the item, with both responding to questions.

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that three letters in support of a review
  and revision of the General Plan; two letters in support of the current
  draft of the East Colorado Specific Plan; three letters providing
  comments related to the Central District; 2 letters expressing
  concerns with the City moving forward with the staff recommended
  changes to the various plans; and one letter in support of staff's
  report on the housing crisis; with all letters received by the City
  Clerk's Office, distributed to the City Council, posted on-line, and
  made part of the public record.

  The following individuals provided comments on the item:

  Anthony Manousos, representing Making Housing and
  Community Happen (MHCH)
  Jasmine Richards Abdullah, representing Black Lives Matter
  Pasadena
  Nina Chomsky, Pasadena resident
  Erika Foy, representing Madison Heights Neighborhood
  Association

  Councilmember Kennedy spoke on the City's need for additional
  tax revenue and to allow development that is consistent with the
  density and height in the surrounding area.

  Councilmember Madison expressed frustration with the state
  lumping Pasadena with other communities who are less focused on
  affordable housing issues, and forcing broad-sweeping mandates
  for residential developments, which will result in negative impacts
  on the quality of life to residents. He strongly advocated for the City
  to join the initiative of other municipalities being circulating related
  to restoring local level zoning control and decision making. He
  spoke in favor of moving forward with a track that would allow the
  City to provide solutions that are best for Pasadena, and resist
  unfunded top-down state mandates.

Council Minutes  11  10/18/2021
   Councilmember Williams supported comments made by
  Councilmember Madison and stated that she believes the best path
  forward is to support the General Plan implementation, Option 2:
  Continue updating the Specific Plans by adjusting densities
  presented in the Round 3 draft Specific Plans to account for a
  potential density bonus, while also taking into consideration
  potential new commercial development. In order to address
  potential concerns over the maximum densities identified in the
  General Plan range, this option would also include a concurrent
  General Plan Amendment to match Specific Plan densities. She
  advocated for the General Plant to be amended in consideration of
  changes in the City (i.e. design guidelines, the acquisition of the 710
  Freeway stub, environmental impacts, empty office space, the
  pandemic, and individuals working from home, etc.).

  Mayor Gordo expressed concerns with the various state initiatives
  that restrict or circumvent local authority; and voiced support for the
  General Plan implementation, Option 2, which will allow the City
  Council to make adjustments to zoning legislation as it is able. He
  requested that Councilmember Madison, Chair of the Legislative
  Policy Committee, agendize for discussion the City joining an
  initiative with other municipalities that is currently being circulated
  related to restoring local zoning control to local officials.

  Vice Mayor Wilson and Councilmembers Rivas and Hampton

 ORDINANCES - FIRST  Conduct first reading of "AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF
READING  PASADENA ADDING SECTION 2.05.230 (NO CAMPAIGN
  CONTRIBUTION LIMIT) TO TITLE 2 (ORGANIZATION AND
  ADMINISTRATION), ARTICLE I (CITY COUNCIL AND ITS
  ADJUNCT RESPONSIBILITIES), CHAPTER 2.05 (CITY
  COUNCIL) TO THE PASADENA MUNICIPAL CODE"

  Mayor Gordo spoke in support of the first reading of the proposed
  ordinance and stated that campaign contribution limits in other
  jurisdictions (i.e. Los Angeles, Los Angeles County) provide
  protections for incumbents, which limits the viability of any real
  campaign challenges to incumbents.

  In response to Councilmember Williams' inquiry related to
  independent expenditures account, City Clerk Jomsky noted that
  his office focuses on candidates and their committees during the
  campaign process, and provided information on the Fair Political
  Practices Commission required forms to be completed related to
  independent expenditures; and responded to questions.

  Councilmember Williams expressed concerns with the barriers and
  lack of transparency that happens when members of the public
  attempt to gather information about independent expenditures.

  Councilmember Rivas spoke in opposition to the proposed
  ordinance related to No Campaign Contribution Limit, stating that
  the current limit of $4,900 is sufficient for Pasadena elections and
  no action will allow the state's campaign contribution limits to remain
  in place.

  Vice Mayor Wilson asked the Ad Hoc Committee to look at what the
  City Council can do to help provide information on independent
  expenditures, strategies other municipalities have implemented,
  including limitations on other financing sources; and additional
  campaign reform measures.

  Chief Assistant City Attorney Javan Rad provided information
  related to the City's ability to restrict independent expenditures; and
  responded to questions.

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that 33 letters (including one letter with
  140 signatures) advocating for campaign finance reform,
  expressing strong concerns and opposition to the propose
  ordinance, and providing comments on the matter, were received
  by the City Clerk's Office, distributed to the City Council, posted on-
  line, and made part of the public record.

  The following individuals spoke in opposition to the first reading of
  the proposed ordinance on No Campaign Contribution Limit:

  At the request of Councilmember Hampton, City Clerk Jomsky,
  provided information on the City's Tax Payer Protection Act (TPA)
  contribution restrictions, tracking, and maintaining TPA reports; and
  responded to questions.

  Councilmember Masuda stated that he supports the state's
  campaign contribution limits.

  Councilmember Madison spoke on the need for staff and the City
  Council to continue to analyze and consider the matter at a future
  Legislative Policy Committee, Ad Hoc Committee, or City Council
  meeting.

  Councilmember Williams noted to include in the discussion the
  timing of any amendments to campaign contribution limits, given
  that the City's 2022 election cycle is starting, with candidates
  already collecting campaign contributions.

  Councilmember Kennedy spoke in support of the proposed
  ordinance, which restores the previous status quo of no limits in
  Pasadena.

Council Minutes  14  10/18/2021
   Councilmember Hampton advocated for the City Council to amend
  the City's TPA provisions to prohibit contributions from any
  employee bargaining unit or major organization (i.e. cannabis and
  large developers organizations); and to legally reduce the number
  of independent expenditures allowed in Pasadena City Council
  elections.

  Following discussion, Councilmember Madison asked staff to
  agendize the matter at the next Legislative Policy Committee.

  Following discussion, on the order of the Mayor, and consensus of
  the City Council, the matter was sent to the Legislative Policy
  Committee for further review.
